title: Budtender Bingo: A Free Dispensary Sales Contest Kit
summary: Free budtender bingo kit: pick specific sales and store goals, print shuffled cards, and run a month-long dispensary sales contest your whole team can win.
body_markdown:
Budtender Bingo is a dispensary sales contest where every square on a 5x5 card is a specific goal, like selling a battery with a cart or completing a cycle count. A manager initials each goal a budtender hits, and five squares in a row wins a prize.


**This guide covers how to pick goals that are specific and verifiable, how to build and print cards with Meadow's free Bingo Card Builder, and how to run the contest on your floor so every budtender, full-time or part-time, has a real shot at winning.**

## Key Takeaways


- A budtender bingo card gives staff 24 specific goals plus a free space, so there are many ways to win instead of one sales number that only top sellers can hit.
- The best bingo goals are countable and easy for a manager to check, like "Opt 3 customers into SMS" or "Cycle count 1 case or 20 products."
- Mixing store operations goals (zero drawer variance, on-time clock-ins, cycle counts) with sales goals rewards the habits that keep a dispensary compliant, not just the register total.
- Goals measured across 3 shifts give part-time budtenders a fair chance to compete alongside full-time staff.
- A month-long contest works well: most budtenders can reach a first BINGO in about 2 weeks, with the rest of the month to chase a full card.


---


## Why Bingo Works Better Than a Single Sales Target


A bingo card works because it gives every budtender several paths to a win, while a single sales target usually rewards the same one or two people every month. When the goal is "highest sales this month," your newest hire and your part-timer know by week one that they are out of the running, and they stop trying.


Bingo spreads the opportunity around. A budtender who is great with first-time customers can knock out the customer squares. Someone who loves the back of house can finish a cycle count and nail their drawer. Each square is small enough to win on a single shift, so people stay engaged for the whole month.


It also lets you reward the work that doesn't show up on a sales leaderboard. Clean drawers, accurate counts, and marketing opt-ins all make your store healthier, and a bingo card puts them on the same level as a big ticket. For more ways to structure rewards, see[Budtender Incentives: Motivate Your Team and Lift Sales](https://getmeadow.com/blog/budtender-incentives) .

## What Goes on a Budtender Bingo Card


A strong budtender bingo card has 24 goals that are specific, countable, and doable within the contest window, plus a free center square. Vague goals like "sell more edibles" or "give great service" create arguments at sign-off. Specific goals like "Sell 2 edibles in 1 sale" don't.


Aim for a mix across five categories so no single type of budtender has an unfair advantage.


**Here's what a good goal looks like, why it's worth a square, and how a manager checks it:**


- **Cycle count 1 case or 20 products.** Keeps inventory accurate between full counts. The manager confirms the completed count in Meadow Admin.
- **Perfect shift: zero drawer variance.** Builds cash-handling discipline. The manager checks the end-of-shift drawer count.
- **Perfect clock-ins for 3 shifts.** Rewards reliability and is fair to part-timers. The manager checks time clock records.
- **Opt 3 customers into SMS.** Grows your text marketing list. The manager checks the opt-in status on each customer profile.
- **Get a 5-star review (show proof).** Builds your online reputation. The budtender shows a screenshot of the review from any platform.
- **Ring 1 $200 sale (tax included).** Encourages full-basket selling. The manager finds the transaction in order history.
- **Sell a battery with a cart 3 times.** Builds a natural add-on habit. The manager checks order history for those sales.


### Store Operations Goals


Store operations goals reward the habits that keep a dispensary compliant and running smoothly. These are the squares that set Budtender Bingo apart from a typical sales contest:


- **Cycle count 1 case or 20 products.** Small enough to finish in one shift, and it keeps your counts current between full inventory audits.
- **Perfect shift: zero drawer variance.** A clean drawer at close is a skill worth rewarding.
- **Perfect clock-ins for 3 shifts.** Three shifts instead of a full week means part-time staff can earn it too.

### Customer Goals


Customer goals reward the conversations that bring shoppers back. Keep the numbers low enough that a budtender can hit them in a few shifts:


- **Opt 3 customers into SMS.** This can happen at intake or at the register.
- **Get a 5-star review (show proof).** Any platform counts, as long as the budtender can show a screenshot.
- **Enroll 3 new loyalty members.**
- **Check out 3 first-time customers.** The SMS square pays off long after the contest ends, because every opt-in is a customer you can reach with your next promotion. Meadow's help center walks through[how to collect marketing opt-ins](https://intercom.help/meadow-admin/en/articles/4613515-how-to-collect-marketing-opt-ins) at intake and checkout.


### Product, Ticket Size, and Upsell Goals


Product, ticket size, and upsell goals are where you steer sales toward what your store wants to move. Name real products and brands, and add a quantity or a condition so the goal is clear:


- **Products and brands:** Sell 1 STIIIZY 1g live resin pod. Sell 3 pre-roll multipacks in 1 shift. Sell the brand of the week 5 times.
- **Ticket size:** Ring 1 $200 sale (tax included). Ring 3 sales of $100+ in 1 shift. Ring a sale with 5+ items.
- **Upsells:** Sell a battery with a cart 3 times. Add-on at checkout 5 times in 1 shift. Upsize 2 customers (8th to quarter, for example).


This is also a natural place to bring in a brand partner. If a vendor wants more shelf attention, ask them to sponsor a square or chip in on the prize.

## How to Run a Budtender Bingo Contest on Your Sales Floor


A budtender bingo contest runs best over one month, with a prize for the first BINGO and a bonus for filling the whole card. That timing gives most budtenders a realistic shot at a first win in about 2 weeks, and the full-card bonus keeps people motivated after their first line.


- **Kick it off at a team huddle.** Hand out cards, explain the prize, and walk through two or three squares so everyone understands what counts.
- **Require manager initials on every square.** A goal only counts once a manager has checked it. This keeps the contest fair and ends "I swear I did it" debates.
- **Post progress where the team can see it.** A simple board in the break room with names and completed lines builds friendly pressure.
- **Celebrate every BINGO.** Call out winners at the next huddle. Recognition matters as much as the prize.
- **Use it for coaching.** Squares that nobody is hitting tell you where your team needs training. Pair the contest with your[new hire training and onboarding plan](https://getmeadow.com/blog/how-to-create-a-new-hire-training-and-onboarding-plan-for-your-dispensary) to close those gaps. ---


## How Managers Verify Each Square


Managers verify budtender bingo squares by checking each goal against a record, not by taking a budtender's word for it. That's why every goal on the card should point to something a manager can look up in a few seconds: a transaction, a customer profile, a completed count, or a screenshot.


Product and ticket-size goals are the easiest to confirm when your POS ties every sale to the budtender who rang it. Operations goals like cycle counts and drawer variance depend on your system recording who did the work and when. Customer goals depend on opt-in and loyalty status living on the customer profile, not on a paper sign-up sheet.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid


The most common budtender bingo mistakes come from goals that are too vague, too hard, or too easy to game. Watch for these when you build your card:


- **Goals nobody can verify.** "Give great service" sounds nice, but a manager can't initial it with confidence. Rewrite it as something countable.
- **Goals that only full-timers can reach.** "Hit your weekly sales goal" shuts out part-timers. "Perfect clock-ins for 3 shifts" doesn't.
- **Goals that reward discounting.** Avoid squares a budtender could hit by giving away margin. Keep an eye on your[discount strategy](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-discount-strategy) while the contest runs.
- **Goals that push against purchase limits.** Big-basket squares should never encourage a sale over your state's limits. Keep ticket goals within normal, compliant transactions.
- **A card that's too hard.** If nobody has a BINGO by the end of week two, swap a few squares for easier ones on the next round.

## Common Questions


### What is budtender bingo?


Budtender bingo is a staff contest where each square on a bingo card is a specific goal, like a sales target, an upsell, or an operations task. A manager initials each square a budtender completes, and five in a row (across, down, or diagonal) wins a prize.


### How long should a dispensary sales contest last?


About one month works well for a bingo-style contest. Most budtenders can reach a first BINGO in roughly 2 weeks, and the rest of the month gives them time to go for a full card and a bonus prize.


### What prizes work for a budtender contest?


Cash bonuses, gift cards, extra paid time off, and first pick of shifts are all popular. Many dispensaries also ask a brand partner to sponsor the prize in exchange for featuring their products on the card.


### How do you keep a budtender contest fair for part-time staff?


Measure goals over a set number of shifts instead of a calendar week. "Perfect clock-ins for 3 shifts" or "3 sales of $100+ in 1 shift" gives a part-timer the same shot at a square as someone working five days.
